evals.prompt: I just fixed a bug in pipeline-manager. Can you rebuild the VSS app images from source so I can redeploy and test the fix locally? I don't need a registry, just local tags.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the VSS app root with the bundled bootstrap helper, changes into it, runs plain `make build` for the application services only, explains that the effective image prefix comes from .env (shipped as intel/) and can be cleared with `REGISTRY_URL= PROJECT_NAME=` for bare local tags, verifies the result, and notes redeploying is handled by vss-deploy/setup.sh using the just-built images.
expectations: The answer runs scripts/vss-bootstrap.sh to resolve APP_ROOT and cd into the VSS app root before building.
The answer uses plain `make build` for the application services and does not run `make build-deps` for a day-to-day app change.
The answer never invokes a top-level ./build.sh - the Makefile is the only build entry point.

The answer explains that no remote registry is needed and that the prefix comes from .env (shipped `intel/`), clearing it with `REGISTRY_URL= PROJECT_NAME=` only if genuinely bare local tags are wanted, and that the build prefix/TAG must match what setup.sh deploys with.
The answer verifies the built images (for example `make list` and/or `docker images | grep -E 'pipeline-manager|vss-ui|video-search|video-ingestion'`).
The answer points deploy follow-up to vss-deploy/setup.sh rather than driving deployment through the build commands.

evals.prompt: This is my first time building VSS from source on this machine. I want all the images built, including the dependency services like multimodal-dataprep, the vector-retriever, and the multimodal embedding service, not just the app ones. What do I need installed and what commands do I run?
evals.expected_output: Explains prerequisites - Docker and make on the host, with poetry NOT required because the embedding-serving image installs it inside the build - resolves and enters the app root, notes that `make build-deps` needs the sibling ../../microservices tree (widening a sparse bootstrap checkout if necessary), runs `make build-deps` and `make build`, and verifies both dependency and application images.
expectations: The answer runs scripts/vss-bootstrap.sh and cd "$APP_ROOT" before invoking any make target.
The answer states Docker and make are required on the host and does not claim host poetry is needed.
The answer runs `make build-deps` for the dependency microservices and `make build` for the application services.
The answer identifies `make build-deps` as building multimodal-dataprep, multimodal-embedding-serving, and the vector-retriever backends (vector-retriever-vdms and vector-retriever-milvus).
The answer notes that `make build-deps` reads the sibling ../../microservices directory and that a sparse bootstrap checkout must be widened (git sparse-checkout add microservices) for it to succeed.
The answer verifies the result with `make list` and/or `docker images | grep -E 'pipeline-manager|vss-ui|video-search|video-ingestion|multimodal-|vector-retriever'`.

evals.prompt: Build the VSS images and push them to our internal registry at `registry.internal.example.com` under the `vss-team` project, tagged `v0.9.2`. I need both the app images and the dependency images pushed so the k8s team can pull them.
evals.expected_output: Sets REGISTRY_URL=registry.internal.example.com, PROJECT_NAME=vss-team, and TAG=v0.9.2 (as make command-line variables or exports), builds application images with `make build` and dependency images with `make build-deps`, then pushes everything with `make push`, verifies the image names, and reminds the user to reuse matching registry/tag values for deployment.
expectations: The answer resolves and enters the app root through scripts/vss-bootstrap.sh before building.
The answer sets REGISTRY_URL=registry.internal.example.com, PROJECT_NAME=vss-team, and TAG=v0.9.2 - as make command-line variables or shell exports, both of which override .env.
The answer builds application images with `make build` and dependency images with `make build-deps` (not a top-level ./build.sh).
The answer uses `make push` to push the built images, and notes it covers both application and dependency images.
The answer mentions matching REGISTRY_URL/PROJECT_NAME/TAG values when deploying with vss-deploy.

evals.prompt: My builds keep failing to reach the internet because we're behind a corporate proxy. Our proxy is `http://proxy.corp.example.com:8080` for both http and https, and I need to bypass it for `localhost` and `.corp.example.com`. Can you build the VSS images with that proxy config applied?
evals.expected_output: Sets http_proxy, https_proxy, and no_proxy in the shell before invoking make, because the Makefile turns non-empty proxy variables into Docker --build-arg values (omitting them entirely when unset), then runs the appropriate make build target and verifies images.
expectations: The answer resolves APP_ROOT with scripts/vss-bootstrap.sh and changes into that directory first.
The answer exports http_proxy and https_proxy to http://proxy.corp.example.com:8080 before running make.
The answer exports no_proxy including localhost, 127.0.0.1, and .corp.example.com before running make.
The answer explains that the Makefile reads inherited proxy env vars and passes them as Docker --build-arg values when non-empty, not via custom proxy flags.
The answer runs `make build` for the application images and only adds `make build-deps` if dependency images are needed.

evals.prompt: I only have this skills folder here, there's no video-search-and-summarization source checked out anywhere on this machine. Please get the source and build the VSS images from scratch for me.
evals.expected_output: Runs the bundled vss-bootstrap.sh from the skill directory to make the source available, explains that absent source triggers a shallow single-branch sparse checkout of only sample-applications/video-search-and-summarization from main, cd's into the resolved app root, runs `make build`, and verifies images.
expectations: The answer runs the bundled scripts/vss-bootstrap.sh helper before any build command.
The answer states that when no checkout is found, the helper performs a shallow, single-branch sparse checkout from main.
The answer states the checkout is limited to sample-applications/video-search-and-summarization rather than the full repository.
The answer changes directory into the resolved APP_ROOT before running `make build`.
The answer mentions VSS_REPO_URL, VSS_REPO_BRANCH, or VSS_CLONE_DIR only as optional bootstrap overrides, not as required flags.

evals.prompt: For our compliance-tagged release, I need the VSS images built with COPYLEFT_SOURCES enabled so the copyleft build-arg is set on every image. Build both the dependency and app images this way, tag them `compliance-2026-07`, and don't push anywhere yet - just confirm locally that they built.
evals.expected_output: Sets ADD_COPYLEFT_SOURCES=true and TAG=compliance-2026-07, builds dependency images with `make build-deps` and application images with `make build` so the copyleft build arg is applied to every image, skips `make push` because the prompt asks for local confirmation only, and verifies local images show the requested tag.
expectations: The answer resolves and cd's into the VSS app root using scripts/vss-bootstrap.sh before building.
The answer sets ADD_COPYLEFT_SOURCES=true (the Makefile knob that injects --build-arg COPYLEFT_SOURCES=true), not a bare COPYLEFT_SOURCES variable.
The answer sets TAG=compliance-2026-07 and does not require a remote REGISTRY_URL or PROJECT_NAME for local confirmation.
The answer runs both `make build-deps` and `make build` so dependency and application images are built.
The answer does not run `make push` because the prompt explicitly says not to push.

evals.prompt: I need to cut a new build of the VSS app images tagged `nightly-2026-07-21`. Just build the app services from source with the default settings, no need to push anywhere - I'll test locally first.
evals.expected_output: Before doing anything else, runs the bundled scripts/vss-bootstrap.sh to resolve the VSS app root, even though the prompt never mentioned setup or cloning. The check inspects the enclosing git repo's remote (origin/upstream) to see if it already points at the official VSS repo or a fork of it, reusing that checkout with no re-clone if so, or otherwise performing a shallow, single-branch, sparse checkout of sample-applications/video-search-and-summarization from main, then cd's into the resolved app root before running `make build TAG=nightly-2026-07-21`.
expectations: The answer runs the bundled bootstrap helper (scripts/vss-bootstrap.sh) as an unconditional first step, before building the requested images, even though the prompt never asked about setup, location, or cloning.

The bootstrap check determines whether the current location is already a valid VSS checkout by inspecting the enclosing git repository's remote configuration (e.g. `git remote -v`, origin/upstream URL) to see if it points at the official open-edge-platform/edge-ai-libraries repo or a fork of it, not merely by checking for local marker files.
If that remote check finds a valid existing checkout (the user's own clone or a fork whose remote traces back to the official repo), the answer reuses it and performs NO re-clone.

If no valid checkout/remote is found, the answer performs a shallow, single-branch, sparse checkout of only sample-applications/video-search-and-summarization from the main branch (not a full-history, all-branches, or full-tree clone).
The answer changes directory into the resolved app root (cd "$APP_ROOT") before running the skill's `make build TAG=nightly-2026-07-21` command for the requested build.
